pages.text: Teinolophos is a small monotreme from the Early Cretaceous of Australia, with an estimated length of only ~15-20 cm. It was discovered in my home state of Victoria, alongside Koolasuchus, Galleonosaurus, and other small monotreme-like mammals such as Ausktribosphenos. This animal is one of our earliest definitive monotremes and an important representative in the diversification of this group.

It would have likely looked reminiscent of modern monotremes, but also quite distinct. Though it lacked a beak, it may have already adapted to a semiaquatic lifestyle, as is presumed to be the ancestral condition for living platypuses and echidnas.
